Research and retry subagents (workbench/briefs/BRIEF-tax.md, BRIEF-tax-retry.md), every quote checked by the lead against its saved page.

figures.finding: A resident pays a flat 10% on all personal income (after his own mandatory social contributions); there is no tax-free allowance and no regional or municipal income tax. Bulgaria uses the euro from 1 January 2026.

sources.said: A flat tax rate of 10% applies to all personal income, with some exceptions.
Individuals must pay personal income tax (PIT) on their gross income less any mandatory social security contributions they make at their own expense. Very few other deductions are possible.
As of 1 January 2026, the euro (EUR) replaces the Bulgarian lev (BGN) as Bulgaria's official currency.

figures.finding: The tax year is the calendar year; the annual return and payment are due by 30 April of the next year, with a 5% discount (capped at EUR 255.65) for filing and paying electronically by 31 March.

sources.said: The tax year in Bulgaria is, without exception, the calendar year.

The deadline for submission of tax returns is 30 April of the following year. A reduction of 5% of the outstanding income tax is applicable if the annual tax return is filed electronically by 31 March of the following year, the individual has no outstanding public liabilities, and the tax is paid by 31 March of the following year. T he discount of 5% is capped at EUR 255.65.

figures.finding: An employee pays 13.78% (10.58% social security, 3.2% health) and the employer 18.92% to 19.62% (the range is the work-accident rate); contributions are on monthly pay up to EUR 2,111.64 (EUR 2,300 from 1 August 2026). A freelancer pays on a chosen monthly base between EUR 550.66 (EUR 620.20 from 1 August 2026) and the same ceiling.

sources.said: The total national insurance contribution rate (social security and health insurance) is 32.7% to 33.4%*, of which 18.92% to 19.62%* is payable by the employer and 13.78% is payable by the employee.

The minimum monthly insurance base for freelancers is EUR 550.66 from 1 January 2026 until 31 July and EUR 620.20 from 1 August 2026 until 31 December 2026. The maximum monthly insurance base for freelancers is EUR 2,111.64 from 1 January 2026 until 31 July, increased to EUR 2,300 effective 1 August 2026.
The maximum monthly insurance base is limited to EUR 2,111.64 from 1 January 2026 until 31 July 2026 and to EUR 2,300 from 1 August 2026 onwards.

figures.finding: The employer withholds the 10% tax from pay monthly and remits it by the 25th of the next month; a Bulgarian payer withholds 10% from a resident freelancer's service fee after a 25% statutory deduction for expenses.

sources.said: Upon payment of salaries, the employer should withhold personal income tax (PIT) at a flat rate of 10% due on employment remuneration, bonuses, and certain fringe benefits and should remit it to the tax authorities by the 25th day of the following month.
to payments to a resident individual (after applying a 25% statutory deduction for expenses).

figures.finding: A resident author's royalties are taxed at 10% after a 40% statutory deduction for expenses (6% effective); royalties to a non-resident bear a final 10%.

Royalties are taxed on an annual basis with a 10% flat tax rate if received by Bulgarian tax residents and a 10% final WHT if received by non-residents.

figures.finding: VAT is 20%; a freelancer must register once taxable turnover exceeds EUR 51,130 in the current or the previous calendar year, within 7 days.

sources.said: A taxable person should register for VAT if its taxable turnover exceeds EUR 51,130 for the current calendar year or for the previous calendar year.
The standard VAT rate is 20%, and the reduced VAT rate is 9%.

figures.finding: A non-resident artiste's (an actor's, director's or other cultural worker's) fee for work done in Bulgaria, even when paid through an agency or production house, is Bulgarian-source income taxed by a final 10% tax on the gross amount, withheld by the payer; an EU or EEA resident may ask for it to be recomputed with the year's return (art. 37a).
